content: For small-tenant multi-tenant systems, Postgres row-level security (RLS) scoped by a tenant/user id pulled from session context is the standard fit (contrasted with schema- or database-per-tenant, reserved for large/regulated tenants). Per-tenant (here per-user) encryption keys are called out as 'gold standard' so a compromise of one key does not expose others — this matches the envelope-encryption decision already made in PROJECT.md. Defense-in-depth: RLS at the DB layer plus query-scoping at the ORM layer plus immutable audit logs on access, not any single layer alone. Source: multiple SaaS engineering blogs (Medium, dev.to, Redis blog) — pattern consensus, not primary spec, MEDIUM.
